result.summary: This PR adds a new functional test, wallet_taproot_decaying_multisig_descriptor_psbt.py, that builds a Taproot version of an existing decaying multisig test: a descriptor combining musig(key1..key4) for the key path with a thresh(...) Miniscript fallback that decays from 4-of-4 to 1-of-4 across future halvening heights. It also adds a documentation section to doc/descriptors.md explaining the new descriptor form and registers the test in test_runner.py. No production code is changed; the PR is test and documentation only.
result.problem: The existing decaying-multisig test only covers a wsh Miniscript construction; there was no test or documentation demonstrating that the same decaying design can be built as a Taproot output using MuSig2 for the common-case key-path spend, which is cheaper and more private. This PR fills that documentation and coverage gap for users or implementers wanting to build such a wallet.

resolved_concerns: rkrux suggested merging this test with the similar wsh test to remove duplicated code; author explained a deliberate preference for keeping tests separate and simple for documentation purposes, and offered to consolidate if others prefer it. No further pushback.

result.card: This PR adds a self-contained functional test and doc example (wallet_taproot_decaying_multisig_descriptor_psbt.py plus a doc/descriptors.md section) demonstrating a Taproot descriptor that combines MuSig2 (for the common 4-of-4 key-path spend) with a Miniscript thresh script-path fallback that decays to 3-of-4, 2-of-4, and 1-of-4 at future halvening heights, mirroring an existing wsh-based decaying-multisig test. It adds no production code; its value is as documentation and integration-test coverage for a fund-safety-conscious pattern (the key path stays spendable after full decay, so a lost key never permanently strands funds). One reviewer gave a Concept ACK and suggested deduplicating with the similar existing wsh test; the author explained a deliberate preference for keeping the tests separate for documentation clarity and offered to reconsider if others agree, and there has been no further pushback. The PR has since gone quiet for over 100 days with no material open question, making it Stale rather than blocked on unresolved disagreement. No dependencies are declared, though the author frames it as the third in a planned three-part series of multisig examples.
